The main takeaway from our work is that

forest islands in a forest-savanna transition zone can be characterized by a continuum in species composition from forest species to savanna species, and that the relative abundance of the different species is determined by their dispersal abilities.
the vegetation of forest patches in the savanna-forest mosaic is determined by a complex interplay of environmental factors (such as soil type and disturbance) and the dispersal abilities of species.
forest islands in the Comoé savanna are not just remnants of a once continuous forest but rather represent a distinct habitat type.
